policy.description: Controlled, auditable platform skips for environment-dependent tests. Every entry must reference a real test id, a real environment signal, and an owner. Skipping is only permitted when the dedicated integration runner does not satisfy the environment requirement; core logic is never skipped. A test path may be listed once per environment; entries must be reviewed by the owner at least every 90 days.
policy.review: owners must re-verify at least every 90 days

environments.description: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner with unprivileged user namespaces enabled and Bubblewrap installed
Dedicated integration runner with full Docker, real Postgres, long-running daemons and network

skips.reason: Bubblewrap (bwrap) must be installed and executable on the runner; the setup step auto-heals by installing it, but a locked-down runner may still lack it. Covers the process sandbox and filesystem/network confinement suites.
Unprivileged user namespaces must be enabled before Bubblewrap can execute; the preparation step performs the sysctl toggle on GitHub runners. Covers the execution sandbox and resource limit suites.
The SDK test matrix runs twice (with and without proxy environment variables) to prove transport neutrality; on a proxy-stripped runner only the explicit variant is authoritative.
Dedicated integration runner is the only environment where the full swarm E2E pipeline exercises real worker daemons and queue draining.
Chaos harness is deliberately excluded from the fast matrix runner because it needs long-running supervisor windows.
Real-system acceptance boot requires a free TCP port and live database adapter; the matrix runner keeps the suite hermetic.
Deploy validation exercises DockerDeployService against a live daemon socket; matrix runner does not expose Docker.
Release executor certification lifecycle drives the real Docker registry contract; matrix runner has no registry.
DR failover verification needs a second writable target; matrix runner is single-node.
Redis task queue and supervised worker loops require a live Redis and long-lived daemons that the matrix runner strips.
Swarm supervisor and worker agent daemons need long-running process windows and real scheduling.
JWT key rotation and re-encryption require the live API runtime boundary.
Tenant RLS enforcement requires the Postgres-backed persistence adapter on the integration runner.
Database queue fencing and runtime primitives exercise durable, real-database semantics (advisory locks, fencing tokens) only available on the integration runner.
